title: Mitigate NTP-induced admission lease drift causing cascading tail latency
creator: Aditi Chandra
description: After two separate enterprise customer escalations on Dedicated and Private deployments, we observed persistent long-context tail latency and queue saturation correlating with maintenance windows that briefly desynchronized host clocks. Root cause analysis points to admission-lease expiry being evaluated against system time (subject to NTP/chrony jitter) which allowed admission windows to slip across hosts. The misalignment created overlapping admission bursts for long-context requests that simultaneously caused KV cache eviction storms and continuous-batcher deadtime, amplifying queue starvation for short requests and causing client timeouts.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a mixed-length workload (90% short requests, 10% long-context generation) to a 4-host private cluster.
2) Introduce a 200-800ms clock step on two of the hosts (simulate NTP drift via chrony step or container shim).
3) Observe admission-lease expiry metrics and admission_token_miss counters in the scheduler telemetry dashboard.
4) Monitor KV cache eviction rate and continuous-batcher idle/unblock cycles; reproduce increased P95/P99 generation latency and 504s from clients.
5) Validate that reverting the clock step restores fair admission; reapply to confirm reproducible spike.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: alert spike at 2026-02-28 04:10 UTC correlating with maintenance window; tenant: ACME-Corp; trace IDs: trace-7f3a, trace-9b2c.
Scheduler logs: admission_lease_expiry evaluated using system clock (time_t) rather than monotonic time; lease handshake had no cross-host jitter damping.
KV cache: concurrent eviction rate increased 6x during admission overlap windows causing hot-eviction churn and increased KV-miss latency.
Batcher behavior: continuous-batcher entered a deadtime loop where long-context batches monopolized GPU windows; small-request starvation persisted for ~12s bursts.
Customer impact: elevated P99 token latency, multiple client SDK retries, two formal support escalations and one SLA credit request.
Hypothesis validated by canary: applying monotonic-time-based expiry prevented the admission overlap even when clock steps were injected.

Trade-offs considered: (a) lengthening admission-grace windows reduces eviction pressure but raises per-tenant latency for extremely long requests; (b) using leader-based global timebase would add cross-host round-trip overhead and complexity.

Decision: implement monotonic-clock evaluation for local lease expiry + admission jitter damping + short grace handshake for inter-host acceptance; backport to dedicated runtime-1.20 and schedule for private on-prem patch release.
resolution: Code patch created to evaluate admission_lease_expiry against a monotonic clock source (runtime monotonic nanoseconds) and introduce a compact inter-host jitter damping window (default 50ms) plus admission-grace extension for active KV handoffs. Deployed hotfix to Hosted canary and three Dedicated customers for verification. Backported minimal patch to runtime-1.20 branch for Private customers and provided Ops runbook to mitigate ongoing escalations.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and run full CI with scheduler unit/integration tests (including synthetic clock skew tests).
2) Deploy to internal canary (hosted): 2 hosts, mixed-length traffic, 48h observation.
3) Gradual rollout to Dedicated customers: start with non-production tenants for 24h, then production tenants with monitoring thresholds gated.
4) Ship backport to Private runtime-1.20 as patch bundle with upgrade instructions and opt-in flag for air-gapped installs.
5) Monitor admission_lease_misalignment, KV_eviction_rate, batcher_starvation_count, and client_504_rate; rollback if >5x baseline for 10m.
prs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 - admission: use monotonic clock and jitter damping
acceptance_criteria: Admission lease expiry is evaluated only against monotonic time in scheduler unit and integration tests.
Synthetic clock skew tests reproduce prior failure before fix and show no admission overlap after fix.
P99 generation latency and KV eviction rates return to baseline in canary and Dedicated customers within 1 hour of rollout.
Ops runbook executed with successful mitigation steps applied to the two escalated customers and confirmed by support.
Customer follow-up: impacted tenants sign off or receive SLA credit where appropriate.
postmortem_action_items: 1) Add NTP drift telemetry and host monotonic/system clock divergence metric to Console (owner: Infra Oncall).
2) Harden scheduler tests: add fuzzed clock-step CI job to catch regressions (owner: Scheduler team).
3) Update private deployment upgrade docs with explicit chrony/ntpd configuration recommendations (owner: Private Delivery).
4) Run a one-time audit of dedicated customer hosts for clock sync health and schedule a maintenance window to apply chrony tuning (owner: Customer Reliability Engineering).
5) Add a low-overhead admission-lease misalignment alert and automated mitigation playbook (owner: SRE).
